verses.text: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

xrefs.text: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.
For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

verses.text: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.

xrefs.text: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share,
He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:
Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

verses.text: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

xrefs.text: For just as rain and snow fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it bud and sprout, and providing seed to sow and food to eat,
If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?
You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it. The streams of God are full of water, for You prepare our grain by providing for the earth.
So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?
Meanwhile, the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall. So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel.

verses.text: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

xrefs.text: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.
Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”

verses.text: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

xrefs.text: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.

I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
How great are Your works, O LORD, how deep are Your thoughts!
O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.

verses.text: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.

xrefs.text: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
For just as rain and snow fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it bud and sprout, and providing seed to sow and food to eat,

You have planted much but harvested little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill. You put on clothes but never get warm. You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.”
Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.
Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

verses.text: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

xrefs.text: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.

verses.text: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.

xrefs.text: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
If only they were wise, they would understand it; they would comprehend their fate.
a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.
In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.

verses.text: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

xrefs.text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is still young.
I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”

verses.text: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.

xrefs.text: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
“Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
